design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (overpayment_waiver_and_recovery).

[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed: {"task": 0, "key": "env_0049_state_unemployment_insurance_agency/overpayment_waiver_and_recovery/0", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 5, 4, 4]}. Assignment: new-plan installment (root) 6 factors, plan reinstatement 4, plan arrears 4, returned-payment fee 5 -> multiset {6,5,4,4}. Task 1 draws 2 prerequisite problems with factor counts [6,5,5] and is reserved for the waiver side of the product (household-income completion, waiver decision, plan change).

[Why this is a good test] A claimant asks for one ordinary thing - a monthly plan on his vacation-pay overpayment. The charter forbids a new plan while another of his plans stands defaulted, a defaulted plan is reinstated only after a repayment covering its arrears, and the arrears are fixed only after every returned repayment carries its fee. None of this is in his request; it is discovered by reading the new-plan rule, seeing the defaulted plan on the older fraud overpayment (find_overpayments), reading the reinstatement rule, then the arrears rule, and seeing on the older ledger that the July 21, 2025 return (LKP-ACH-2507150276) has no fee entry. Each problem then needs its own multi-factor arithmetic over the ledger, the plan fields, the tier parameters and the withholding/claim records of other products. Difficulty is reading policy, querying the world and calculating; there is one tool per problem and no near-synonym tools.

[Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed by this task: policies overpay_ext_returned_payment_fee, overpay_ext_plan_arrears, overpay_ext_plan_reinstatement, overpay_ext_new_plan_installment; tools book_returned_payment_fee_10cb479c (agent), pay_overpayment_arrears_d9b1e543 (user), reinstate_repayment_plan_54c54ed5 (user), set_up_repayment_plan_0b609272 (user). Left for task 1 (independent and load-bearing): the waiver chain - completing a lodged waiver request's household income (user), the waiver decision and principal adjustment (agent), and the change of an existing plan after the waiver (user) - none of which this task touches. Events of this difficulty used here: overpay_fee_assessed, overpay_repayment_received (penalty component only: a principal repayment would trigger charge:charge_credit_reversed in another category, so the arrears tool books only the penalty component), overpay_repayment_plan_set.

[Problem-tree card] Root: overpay_ext_new_plan_installment (set_up_repayment_plan_0b609272, owner user). Chain:
 (e1) new plan -> reinstatement: kind state_gate, gate overpayments.repayment_plan_status, form state, sentence "A new repayment plan is set only after none of the claimant's other overpayments carries a repayment plan whose status is defaulted." Four-point test: ordering connective "only after"; record-visible state (plan status on the other overpayments); no tool/id/code token; scope "none of the other overpayments", hard requirement. The only write in this difficulty that turns a defaulted status to current is the reinstatement tool (the arrears and fee writes do not touch plan status; set-up acts on a plan-less overpayment). False at opening: initial_state.overpayments.6ce505f1-7de7-4c69-b966-fa9feb6bca1c.repayment_plan_status = defaulted.
 (e2) reinstatement -> arrears: kind value_input, gate balance, form state, negated direction, sentence "A defaulted plan is not reinstated until a repayment at least equal to the arrears payment worked out for it has been booked on the overpayment after the plan's most recent returned installment." The only write booking a repayment is the arrears payment tool. False at opening: last return initial_state.overpay_ledger.0b0d8ddf-99aa-4b02-b27b-4cf9ed574678 dated 2025-07-21, last repayment 2025-07-15 (returned). Load: skip -> reinstated installment 71.72 instead of 60.22.
 (e3) arrears -> fee: kind value_input, gate fees_in_arrears, form state, affirmative, sentence "The arrears payment on a defaulted plan is fixed only after the overpayment's ledger carries a returned-payment fee for every repayment returned unpaid on it." Only the fee tool writes fee entries. False at opening: initial_state.overpay_ledger.0b0d8ddf-99aa-4b02-b27b-4cf9ed574678 (LKP-ACH-2507150276) has no fee; the two fee entries carry LKP-ACH-2502036614 and LKP-ACH-2506138391. Load: skip -> arrears 87.00 instead of 138.00.
 Topological order fee -> arrears -> reinstatement -> new plan (steps 6, 8, 10, 15). Value-input edges 2 (>= max(3-1,1)). Owner=user problems: arrears payment, reinstatement and the root plan (all three are the claimant agreeing to pay or to a plan); the fee is the Department's own booking. The sentences run in both directions (affirmative for the new plan and arrears, negated for the reinstatement), each the way the desk states it. user_scenario names no prerequisite; the older plan appears only in reactions conditioned on the representative raising it. The tools validate nothing (see prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block).

[Base-invariant card] fee (subject overpay_fee_assessed): governing overpay_evt_penalty_interest; its only gate (interest_once_per_month) applies to interest, so policy_scope; overwrite declared on "A repayment returned unpaid by the bank reverses its application and is followed by the returned-payment fee, which is booked as its own fee component." (base fee is the flat classification fee 25.00; the extended fee is 51.00 here). arrears (subject overpay_repayment_received): governing overpay_agg_recovery_priority (no gate; designated repayment applied to the named overpayment) and overpay_evt_recovery gate voluntary_repayment_on_open_debt - status in_recovery is allowed (initial_state.overpayments.6ce505f1-7de7-4c69-b966-fa9feb6bca1c.status = in_recovery). reinstatement and new plan (subject overpay_repayment_plan_set): overpay_repayment_plan gate plan_on_open_debt - status in_recovery for both overpayments; overwrite declared on the base installment sentence (both policies replace "balance / maximum plan months, at least the minimum" with their own month counts; the base minimum stays as the floor). No time gate applies to these subjects, so temporal_feasibility is empty.

[Business-object card] Older overpayment 6ce505f1-7de7-4c69-b966-fa9feb6bca1c (Fraud Overpayment - First Offense, claim d82171dd-16f0-467b-80ae-9394232ab7d1, determined 2024-04-08, principal 4,906.00 fully intercepted 2025-03-04, penalty 735.90 of which 521.90 unpaid, interest 441.54 unpaid, fees 36.00 + 36.00 unpaid, plan 60.00/month first due 2025-05-16, defaulted, notice of intent 2025-09-22). Returns: 2025-02-07 (LKP-ACH-2502036614, pre-plan, fee 36.00), 2025-06-18 (LKP-ACH-2506138391, fee 36.00, replaced by card 2025-06-20), 2025-07-21 (LKP-ACH-2507150276, no fee - the object of step 6). Vacation-pay overpayment cfe2f8c0-5554-4418-ad06-cb1c7e1ba493 (Claimant Error, other pay unreported, weeks 2023-11-25..2023-12-30, principal 2,676.00, determined 2025-01-13, in recovery, repayments 200.00 card 2025-03-03, 150.00 ACH 2025-04-07 returned 2025-04-11 with fee 36.00, 100.00 card 2025-08-18, balance 2,412.00, no plan) - the object of the root. Each fee/return/repayment is tied to its source by payment_reference; the intercept by intercept_reference TOP 25064 0304 778126. The arrears and reinstatement act only on 6ce505f1-7de7-4c69-b966-fa9feb6bca1c; the new plan only on cfe2f8c0-5554-4418-ad06-cb1c7e1ba493.

[Factor card] (tier taken / baseline result from the Step 5 run)
 fee 51.00 (baseline 25.00): face_amount_tier middle tier 30.00 (46.00); repeat_return_surcharge one other return +10.00 (41.00); return_lookback_window anchored at the plan's first installment due date 2025-05-16 (4 + 1 = 5 months), the 2025-02-07 return falls outside (56.00 with 12 months) - near-miss: a careless reader counts the February return; depository_bank_charge ACH +6.00 (45.00); late_return_handling 6-day return +5.00 (46.00) - near-miss: the June return took 5 days and earned nothing.
 arrears 138.00 (baseline 180.00): default_age_cutoff 85 days -> count to the July return, 3 installments (188.00); breakdown_timing_price 2 months -> minimum 50.00 (153.00); support_obligation_share [multi-source, cross-difficulty withhold] child support 92.00/week AND active SNAP recovery order -> 0.50 (153.00); returned_installment_fees two returned installments -> all unpaid fees 123.00 (15.00) - near-miss: the February fee is pre-plan but still "standing unpaid" and joins.
 reinstatement 60.22 (baseline 50.00): returned_installment_months 18 (50.00); defaulted_plan_end_anchor take off 4 months (55.52); intercept_relief 5,000.00 intercepted in 12 months +6 (72.32); fraud_penalty_schedule first-offense penalty over 12 months (50.00).
 new plan 100.50 (baseline 50.25): principal_size_months 36 (67.00); establishment_delay_extension +3 (114.86); determination_date_anchor -9 (73.10); good_faith_payment +3 (114.86); returned_payment_history -6 (80.40); return_to_work [cross-difficulty claim] last benefit 2024-03-19 -> -3 (89.34) - the claim ledger, not the profile, decides it.
 Every factor's tier rests on ledger rows, dates or other-product records; no stamp is read (repayment_plan_status is the gate of e1 and the plan-status test of the look-back anchor, never an outcome stamp). Each extended number is a policy param; each base figure (returned_payment_fee, min_monthly_payment, max_plan_months) is read with P().

[World rows] customer 79b24095-85ec-4dd2-b7da-9f12879ee429; claim d82171dd-16f0-467b-80ae-9394232ab7d1 with entitlement credit, waiting week and 23 weekly payments 2023-10-14..2024-03-16 (remaining 1,338.00) - the last payment 2024-03-19 drives return_to_work; withholding orders 324fc364-c7af-48c0-9280-30824eb9638f (child support 92.00/week, active) and eb39a5e0-183e-41ec-a67e-143ea9e0d5ff (SNAP household-error recovery, certified 860.00, active) drive the obligation share; overpayments 6ce505f1-7de7-4c69-b966-fa9feb6bca1c and cfe2f8c0-5554-4418-ad06-cb1c7e1ba493 with 29 ledger rows. Removing the July return removes the fee obligation and the default; removing the intercept removes intercept relief and leaves principal unpaid (arrears would be zero); removing the withholding orders moves the share to 1.

[Persona design] A tired mechanic on his lunch break, short sentences, gives details only when asked; volunteers only the surface goal (plan on the vacation-pay overpayment). Conditional reactions: accepts bringing the older plan current and pays the stated amount by debit card when handed the step; agrees to put the older plan back in place at the stated amount; agrees to the new plan as given; declines extra payment; ends after confirmation. He never proposes figures or asks for anything the charter does not decide.

[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify (phone, SSN last4, DOB) -> find_overpayments -> find_overpay_ledger(older) -> find_withholding_orders -> unlock/call fee 51.00 -> unlock/call arrears 138.00 (user) -> unlock/call reinstatement 60.22 (user) -> find_overpay_ledger(vacation-pay) -> find_claims -> find_claim_ledger -> unlock/call new plan 100.50 (user).

[Verification] Values recomputed with the gate engine on the handling-time worlds (initial_state + earlier gold writes replayed through the real tools): fee 51.0, arrears 138.0, reinstatement 60.22, new plan 100.5; prerequisite skips: arrears without fee 87.0, reinstatement without arrears 71.72, new plan without reinstatement 100.5 (gate edge, terminal plan status differs). Gate runs are recorded below.

[Gate runs — final, difficulty-wide, repository root]

check_task_tools.py -> TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK (7 tools).
replay_tasks.py -> 0.json 16 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous, 0 errors, closure 60 = initial 60; REPLAY OK.
check_solvability.py -> 0.json verify True, 4 calls, 5 base gates, 31 seed rows; SOLVABILITY OK.
check_compute.py -> 0.json 4 computations, 19 factors, 2 cross-difficulty, history rows 35, branches 58, 16 steps, match True; suite means branches 64.50 / steps 16.00, history max 35, branch max 71; COMPUTE OK.
check_grounding.py -> GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire.py -> SCOPE OK; check_cache_diff.py -> INFO only (no cache trap used).
validate_scenario -> the only errors for this difficulty are "required document ... not found" for the four policy ids, which the KB render will publish; no forbidden-token, rw or frozen_time error.

[Manual value gates] Length/breadth: request (plan on the vacation-pay overpayment) -> defaulted plan on the other overpayment (new-plan sentence) -> arrears repayment (reinstatement sentence) -> fee for the unfeed return (arrears sentence); breadth over ledger history, plan fields, tier parameters, withholding orders and claim payments. Every owner=user problem is something only the claimant can do (pay, agree to a plan) and completes on the call. Persona: goal and identity only; reactions fire on the representative's explanations; no prerequisite named. Chronology: every volunteered fact (vacation-pay overpayment from late 2023, paying by card now and then, back at work) is in initial_state. No time gate applies; no real-world wait: the card payment is taken on the call, the plan writes are immediate. Rule/compute two-way: each ladder is stated tier by tier in its rule and quoted in compute_basis; every factor's baseline is the computation document's standard method. Draft recomputation from the visible text alone reproduces 51.00 / 138.00 / 60.22 / 100.50 with the reads listed in the standard solution.


[Rework round 2 — policy-task audit items] G-1/F0-1: return_lookback_window is now a genuine anchor method (anchor at the plan's first installment due date for a current/defaulted plan whose first due date has passed; anchor at the determination date for a fraud overpayment without such a plan; otherwise the standard 12 months back from the handling date); params lookback_months_plan/lookback_months_fraud removed. Here: anchored at 2025-05-16, 4 + 1 = 5 months, fee stays 51.00, baseline 12 months 56.00. Seed re-derived under the revised rule: the June fee (0063dbe4…) is 36.00 (its plan-anchored look-back leaves out the pre-plan February return), so balance_due of 6ce505f1… is 1,035.44; arrears 15.00 + fees 36.00 + 36.00 + 51.00 = 138.00; reinstated installment 383.90 / 12 + (948.44 - 383.90) / 20 = 60.2187 -> 60.22; skip figures: arrears without fee 87.00, reinstatement without arrears 71.72; arrears receipt LKP-CC-a0c644057ad0. G-3: the look-back plan test reads status current or defaulted (no longer != none). G-4: the rule counts and prices by return entry. O-1: fee overwrite replaced_by is the composite fee sentence. O-2/F0-4: the late-return charge is stated as the depository's late-presentment/dispute handling cost. G-2: reinstatement, new-plan and plan-change month ladders are shares of the classification maximum (0.50/0.75, 0.50/0.75, 0.20/0.40), so every tier is distinct for every classification; here 18 = 0.50 x 36 and 36 = 0.75 x 48, values unchanged. G-9/F0-2: the new-plan returned-payment sentence is scoped to return entries on the overpayment. F0-3: the SNAP order eb39a5e0… now carries claim_id null (no claim was open when it arrived in June 2025). Ledger row count corrected: the two overpayments carry 29 ledger rows. All gates re-run green.

[Rework round 3 — revision_2 audit items] R2-G-10: the fee rule's plan-anchored look-back no longer adds the clause about returns from before the plan, and the ladder texts now state each anchor as the whole months elapsed from the anchor date to the handling date plus the month in progress, the same whole-months test the compute applies. On this world the window is still MONTHS(2025-05-16, 2025-10-14) + 1 = 5 and the 2025-02-07 return (8 whole months back) stays outside; every value of this task is unchanged (51.00 / 138.00 / 60.22 / 100.50).
user_scenario:
You are Thaddeus Okonkwo-Brandvold, a 45-year-old maintenance mechanic in Ashby Falls, calling the Lakeland Department of Workforce Security on your lunch break. You went back to full-time work in early 2024 after a stretch on unemployment, and you still owe on an overpayment about vacation pay from your old job at the foundry, the weeks at the end of 2023 when the vacation payout was not reported on your claim. You have been paying on it now and then by card, but you want to set up monthly payments on it so it stops hanging over you. You do not know the exact balance and you want the Department to work out the monthly amount; you are ready to agree to a plan today over the phone.

You speak plainly and a little wearily, in short sentences, and you give your details only when the representative asks for them: your phone number is 6085552417, the last four digits of your Social Security number are 2638, your date of birth is 1979-11-23, your ZIP code is 53726, and your email is thaddeus.okonkwobrandvold@gmail.com. If you are asked which overpayment you mean, it is the one about the vacation pay from the foundry at the end of 2023.

If the representative brings up another overpayment or an older payment plan, you remember that there was one from early 2024 that you were paying monthly until money got tight over the summer, but you do not know where it stands now. If the representative explains that the older plan has to be brought current before a new plan can be set up, you accept that, saying you would rather sort it out now than have it hanging over you, and when they tell you the amount and hand you the payment step you pay exactly that amount on your debit card right away. If they then tell you the older plan can be put back in place at a monthly amount they give you, you agree to put it back in place at that amount. You never suggest amounts yourself, you do not ask for any discount, forgiveness or extra time, and you do not dispute the figures you are given.

When the representative tells you the monthly amount for the vacation-pay overpayment and hands you the step to agree to it, you agree to the plan as given. If they ask whether you want to pay anything extra today on the vacation-pay overpayment, you say no, the plan is enough. As soon as they confirm the new plan is set up, you thank them and end the call.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.overpayment_id: 6ce505f1-7de7-4c69-b966-fa9feb6bca1c. Basis: the fee is "booked once, as its own fee component, on the same overpayment" (policy rule) and the returned repayment LKP-ACH-2507150276 sits on the older fraud overpayment row returned by find_overpayments. Uniqueness: the vacation-pay overpayment has only one return (April 2025), which already carries its fee; only the older overpayment has a return without a fee.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_reference: LKP-ACH-2507150276. Basis: "The return being charged is the most recent repayment on the overpayment that was returned unpaid, identified by the confirmation number on its return entry." The most recent return entry on the older overpayment is dated 2025-07-21 with payment_reference LKP-ACH-2507150276 (find_overpay_ledger). Uniqueness: the two earlier returns (LKP-ACH-2502036614, LKP-ACH-2506138391) already have fee entries; the tool docstring requires the confirmation number copied exactly.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.fee_amount: 51.00. Face-amount tier: returned amount 60.00 is above the lower face-amount threshold 50.00 and not above 300.00 -> middle-tier face charge 30.00 (baseline would be the classification fee 25.00). Look-back window (method): the overpayment carries a defaulted plan whose first installment due date 2025-05-16 has passed -> the look-back is anchored at that date and covers MONTHS(2025-05-16, 2025-10-14) = 4 whole months plus the month in progress = 5 months, which takes the returns of 2025-06-18 and 2025-07-21 but not the pre-plan return of 2025-02-07 (8 whole months back) -> one other return (the standard 12-month look-back from the handling date would see two). Repeat surcharge: one other return -> single-return surcharge 10.00. Bank charge: the original repayment LKP-ACH-2507150276 was online_ach -> ACH-debit bank charge 6.00. Late return: received 2025-07-15, return booked 2025-07-21 = 6 days, more than 5 and not more than 10 -> late-return charge 5.00. Sum 30 + 10 + 6 + 5 = 51.00, rounded to the cent.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: Produced by overpay_ext_plan_arrears: installments counted 3 (default dated by the 2025-07-21 return, 85 days before handling, more than 60 -> count up to that return) priced at the classification minimum 50.00 (plan broke down 2 whole months after its first due date, fewer than 6) = 150.00 less the installment credit 120.00 = 30.00, times the two-obligation share 0.50 = 15.00, plus every unpaid returned-payment fee 36.00 + 36.00 + 51.00 = 123.00 (two plan installments returned), = 138.00, within the unpaid penalty 521.90.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.overpayment_id: 6ce505f1-7de7-4c69-b966-fa9feb6bca1c. Basis: the arrears payment is "the claimant's own repayment, designated to that overpayment" whose plan has defaulted; find_overpayments shows only the older fraud overpayment with repayment_plan_status defaulted. Uniqueness: the vacation-pay overpayment has no plan at all, so it has no arrears.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 138.00. Default-age cutoff (method): most recent returned installment booked 2025-07-21, 85 days before 2025-10-14 (more than the long default-age days 60) -> installments counted = 1 + whole months from 2025-05-16 to 2025-07-21 (2) = 3, instead of 1 + 4 = 5 to the handling date. Breakdown pricing: 2 whole months from first due date to that return, fewer than 6 -> each priced at the classification minimum 50.00 instead of the plan installment 60.00. Installment credit: repayments 2025-05-15 60 + 2025-06-13 60 + 2025-06-20 60 + 2025-07-15 60 less returns 2025-06-18 60 + 2025-07-21 60 = 120.00 (entries within 4 + 1 whole months back). Installment part 3 x 50 - 120 = 30.00. Support-obligation share (cross-difficulty, withholding records): current child-support order 92.00 a week (at least 75.00) and an active SNAP household-error recovery order -> two-obligation share 0.50 -> 15.00. Returned-installment fees: two returns among the credit entries -> every unpaid returned-payment fee joins: fees booked 36.00 + 36.00 + 51.00 (booked at step 6) = 123.00, no fee-component repayments. Arrears 15.00 + 123.00 = 138.00, not above the penalty standing unpaid 521.90 (principal fully recovered by the 2025-03-04 intercept).

argument_uniqueness_tracing.overpayment_id: cfe2f8c0-5554-4418-ad06-cb1c7e1ba493. argument_uniqueness_tracing.monthly_amount: 100.50. Balance 2,412.00 (2,676.00 - 200.00 - 100.00 + 36.00 fee; the returned 150.00 was reversed). Principal-size months: principal established 2,676.00 is above the small-principal cap 1,500.00 and up to 5,000.00 -> mid-principal share 0.75 of the classification maximum 48 = 36 (baseline 48). Establishment delay: whole months from the last overpaid week 2023-12-30 to the determination 2025-01-13 = 12 -> at least 12, fewer than 18 -> +3. Good faith: most recent repayment 2025-08-18, 57 days before 2025-10-14, within 90 -> +3. Determination anchor (method): 9 whole months from 2025-01-13 to 2025-10-14, more than 6 -> take off all 9. edges.condition: No other overpayments row of the same customer has repayment_plan_status defaulted.
edges.policy_source: A new repayment plan is set only after none of the claimant's other overpayments carries a repayment plan whose status is defaulted.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At frozen time the claimant's other overpayment carries a repayment plan whose status is defaulted, so the gate "none of the claimant's other overpayments carries a repayment plan whose status is defaulted" is false.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 10 (reinstate_repayment_plan_54c54ed5) sets the older overpayment's repayment_plan_status to current with monthly amount 60.22, so no other overpayment of the claimant carries a defaulted plan when step 15 runs.

edges.condition: The overpay_ledger carries an overpay_repayment_received entry dated after the latest overpay_repayment_returned entry whose amount is at least the arrears payment, and overpayments.balance_due reflects it.
edges.policy_source: A defaulted plan is not reinstated until a repayment at least equal to the arrears payment worked out for it has been booked on the overpayment after the plan's most recent returned installment.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The most recent returned installment on the older overpayment was booked 2025-07-21 and the last repayment on the ledger is the returned 2025-07-15 installment; no repayment has been booked after the return, let alone one covering the arrears.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 8 (pay_overpayment_arrears_d9b1e543) books a 138.00 repayment dated 2025-10-14 (LKP-CC-a0c644057ad0) on the older overpayment and lowers its balance due to 948.44, the balance the reinstated installment is computed on.

edges.condition: Every overpay_repayment_returned entry on the overpayment has an overpay_fee_assessed entry carrying the same payment_reference.
edges.policy_source: The arrears payment on a defaulted plan is fixed only after the overpayment's ledger carries a returned-payment fee for every repayment returned unpaid on it.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The return entry of the July installment (payment_reference LKP-ACH-2507150276) has no fee entry: the only fee entries on the older overpayment carry LKP-ACH-2502036614 and LKP-ACH-2506138391.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 6 (book_returned_payment_fee_10cb479c) books the 51.00 fee with payment_reference LKP-ACH-2507150276, so every returned repayment on the overpayment carries a fee and the unpaid fees joining the arrears become 123.00.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain (fee -> arrears -> reinstatement -> new plan); every edge is stated by a prerequisite sentence, so the four writes have exactly one order. No two writes are parallel prerequisites of the same problem, so no commuting argument is needed.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the reinstatement leaves the new-plan installment at 100.50 (it is computed from the vacation-pay overpayment's own records) but the terminal state differs: the older overpayment keeps repayment_plan_status defaulted and monthly amount 60.00 instead of current / 60.22, and the gate of the new plan stays false.
Skipping the arrears payment leaves the balance at 1,086.44 and the unpaid penalty at 521.90, so the reinstated installment becomes 71.72 instead of 60.22 and no 138.00 repayment is booked.
Skipping the fee booking leaves the unpaid fees at 72.00, so the arrears payment becomes 87.00 instead of 138.00 (and the fee entry and the 51.00 balance increase are missing).

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The customer asks only to set up monthly payments on the vacation-pay overpayment. The user_scenario never names the fee, the arrears, the reinstatement or any policy id, and never volunteers the older overpayment: it mentions the older plan only inside conditional reactions that fire after the representative brings it up ("If the representative brings up another overpayment or an older payment plan ..."). He never suggests amounts or steps.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: None of the four task tools checks a prerequisite: book_returned_payment_fee_10cb479c, pay_overpayment_arrears_d9b1e543, reinstate_repayment_plan_54c54ed5 and set_up_repayment_plan_0b609272 only look the overpayment up by id (returning an error only for an unknown id) and then write exactly what they are given; set_up_repayment_plan_0b609272 would set the new plan even while another plan stands defaulted, and reinstate_repayment_plan_54c54ed5 would reinstate without any arrears payment. The consequence of a skipped prerequisite shows only in the terminal hash.
